svg.title: danielgarcia.it: how the pages are built from the data
svg.text: Overview: how the pages are built from the data
Everything happens at build time. Details in two other diagrams: yaml-to-java-records.svg and page-rendering-and-i18n.svg.
texts, one YAML file per language
labels and addresses of the interface
Same keys, same entries, same order
a missing key, a date in the wrong
One record per language, a CDI
Qute templates, one per part of a page
Each partial reads its data in the
language of the page, then loops
the pages: front matter, then includes
en/… the same pages in English
The home page also holds the
i18n: read without a record, straight into the partials
opens the large card of a card
compact profile once the profile is gone
the one skeleton around every page
<head>: title (page title — name, or name — job title on the home page), description
{#bundle /}: the scripts of web/, bundled by the Web Bundler (static/bundle/app-<hash>.js)
{#include partials/header /}: skip link, compact profile, menu, FR | EN
<main id="content">{#insert /}</main>: the body of the page from content/
{#include partials/footer /}: source code of the site, privacy page
<html lang="{page.data.lang}">: French or English for the browser and screen readers
Both languages exist and have the same shape: same entries, same order, same shared details.
Never the wording: a sentence can change without touching a test.
the generated pages, served as in production, in both languages
Sections by their ids, links to the CV and between pages, header and footer on every page,
then every internal link of the generated site. A failure blocks the image and the release.
